# How on time are Island Transit's buses?

[Every few seconds, each Island Transit bus reports where it is, and each
report vanishes as soon as the next one arrives. This site saves all of them
and uses them to figure out how often the buses leave on time.]{.lede}

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
STATUS_URL = "https://ekczqlmunyumtgtthppb.supabase.co/rest/v1/status_now"
PUBLIC_KEY = "sb_publishable_AWlvBYVrlTz7dEaf7RwwzA_5zRN3af-"
status = {
  try {
    const r = await fetch(STATUS_URL, {headers: {apikey: PUBLIC_KEY}});
    return r.ok ? await r.json() : null;
  } catch (e) { return null; }
}
vp = status?.find(d => d.feed === "vehiclePositions") ?? null
ago = s => s < 120 ? `${s} second${s === 1 ? "" : "s"} ago` : s < 7200 ? `${Math.round(s / 60)} minutes ago` : `${Math.round(s / 3600)} hours ago`
html`${vp == null
  ? html`<a class="live" href="#how-it-works"><span class="dot"></span>Saving bus locations every 20 seconds</a>`
  : vp.last_ok_age_s < 120
    ? html`<a class="live ok" href="#how-it-works"><span class="dot"></span>Saving now · last update ${ago(vp.last_ok_age_s)}</a>`
    : html`<a class="live down" href="#how-it-works"><span class="dot"></span>Collector delayed · last update ${ago(vp.last_ok_age_s)}</a>`}`
```
:::

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
import {csv, json, pct, lateness, plural, longDate, routeMap, routeSlug} from "./lib.js"
import {drawRouteMap} from "./map.js"
recent = json("data/ontime/recent.json")
quality = csv(d3, "data/quality/daily.csv")
q = quality.at(-1) ?? null
o = recent?.overall ?? null
period = recent == null ? "" : recent.days === 1
  ? `on ${longDate(recent.last_service_date)}`
  : `over the ${recent.days} days to ${longDate(recent.last_service_date)}`
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
html`${o == null || o.observed === 0
  ? html`<p class="empty">The first numbers will show up here shortly after midnight Pacific, once the first full day has been processed.</p>`
  : html`<div class="headline">
      <div class="big">${pct(o.on_time_share_of_observed)}</div>
      <div class="big-label">of departures left on time ${period}.
        <span class="note">A bus counts as on time if it leaves no more than 1 minute early or 5 minutes late.</span></div>
    </div>
    <div class="stat-row">
      <div class="stat"><div class="label">Typical departure</div>
        <div class="value">${lateness(o.deviation_s_median)}</div></div>
      <div class="stat"><div class="label">More than 5 minutes late</div>
        <div class="value">${pct(o.late_share_of_observed)}</div></div>
      <div class="stat"><div class="label">Departures checked</div>
        <div class="value">${o.observed.toLocaleString("en-US")}</div></div>
    </div>`}`
```

## Every route at a glance

Pick any route on the map to see how it did at each stop.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
html`<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/leaflet@1.9.4/dist/leaflet.css">`
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
L = require("leaflet@1.9.4")
mapData = routeMap(recent?.timepoints)
homeMap = mapData == null ? null : drawRouteMap(L, mapData, recent, {
  height: width < 640 ? 440 : 640,
  onSelect: id => {
    const r = mapData.routes.find(r => r.route_id === id);
    location.href = `routes.html#${routeSlug(r, id)}`;
  },
})
html`${homeMap == null ? html`<p class="empty">The route map will appear once the first day has been processed.</p>` : homeMap.node}`
```

::: {.how-steps}
Each bus carries a GPS unit that reports where it is. Island Transit passes
those reports along to trip-planning apps through a live feed, and every new
update wipes out the one before it. Every 20 seconds, day and night, our
collector asks the feed for its latest update and saves it. Each night, our
script turns the saved updates into the charts, the map and the files you
can download here.
:::
:::

The feed tells us where a bus is, but it never says when the bus left a
stop. So the script traces every bus along its route, finds the moment it
passed each stop, and compares that moment with the printed timetable. The
same saved data also shows how often the tracking itself breaks down, which
you can see on the [Data quality](quality.qmd) page.

## Why this exists

Island Transit doesn't publish on-time figures, and once the live feed moves
on, its data is gone for good. Saving it lets anyone ask "Was route 60 late
last week?" and check the code behind the answer.
